# 4. The service worker is hand-written, not generated by Workbox

Date: 2026-09-17

## Status

Accepted.

## Context

The application must open and work with no connectivity, which is its normal resting
state. Until now that has only been true on the development machine, because nothing
made the shell, scripts, styles, and fonts available without a network. A service
worker that precaches those at install and serves them from the cache afterwards is
what makes the claim true on a tablet in a school.

What it must do is small and fixed: precache the build's files (the HTML shell, the
hashed JavaScript and CSS, the four font files, the icons and manifest); serve
navigations and those files cache-first; never cache API calls (there are none yet;
they will be network-only); delete old caches when a new build activates; and tell
the user a new version is ready rather than swapping it under them mid-marking.

The usual route is `vite-plugin-pwa`, which generates a Workbox service worker. It is
convenient, but the worker it produces is not ours, its runtime is sizeable, and the
developers must be able to explain every part of this system at an oral examination.

## Decision

The service worker is written by hand in `frontend/src/sw.js`, about eighty lines of
plain JavaScript with no build step of its own. A small Vite plugin of our own
(`frontend/build/precache.ts`) fills in the list of the build's files as the precache
manifest and a version hashed from the files' contents, then emits it at the site
root, so the list is visible in the build output and the version changes whenever
anything in it does. Registration and the "update ready" prompt live in
`frontend/src/lib/serviceWorker.ts`; the worker only activates on the user's say-so
(`SKIP_WAITING`), then the page reloads onto the new version.

Caching rules, in order: requests under `/api/` go to the network and are never
cached; navigations are answered with the cached shell (so a reload offline works);
same-origin files in the manifest are cache-first; anything else is network with a
cache fallback. Only production builds register a worker; development unregisters
any it finds so the dev server's live reload is not fought.

## Consequences

- Every line of the offline behaviour is in the repository and explainable.
- The precache list is generated, never hand-maintained, so a new font or chunk is
  cached without anyone remembering to add it.
- No background sync, push notifications, or routing rules beyond those above. Any of
  those is the reason to revisit this decision and take Workbox, in a later ADR.
- A web app manifest and icons make the app installable; the fonts rule in AGENTS.md
  (self-hosted, precached) is now enforced by the build rather than by discipline.
